scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1,240 ESTIMATED, 1,785 ACTUAL (billing-db).

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1,240 ESTIMATED, 1,785 ACTUAL (billing-db).

F-03.statement: Billing-db tariff change log returned 0 records: no tariff changes logged.

F-04.statement: Field route completion Aug-Sep: 0.88 actual vs 0.95 target, 9,200 manual read accounts affected (route-log).

F-05.statement: Dispute ticket response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA, across 2,440 tickets (crm-tickets).

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request field route priority changes, which are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-capacity problem, solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets, independent of why bills are actually wrong.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused reads or estimates to be misclassified, producing incorrect bills and the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: The MDMS nightly export of AMI reads (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or degrading since August, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter-read completion (contracted via ORG-FIELD) dropped since August, increasing missed reads and estimate substitutions that generated wrong bills.

H-HANDOFF-SEMANTIC-MISMATCH.statement: A semantic/format defect in one of the data handoffs (H-FIELD-BILL or H-MDMS-BILL) into billing import is silently corrupting read values independent of rule changes, vendor outages, or staffing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills, 1,240 used ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 used ACTUAL reads — the majority (about 59%) of disputes stem from bills built on real meter reads, not substituted estimates. This weakens explanations centered on rising estimate substitution and favors a cause that corrupts or misclassifies both read types (e.g. a billing rule or tariff defect).

The tariff change log shows zero records, meaning there were no tariff rate changes logged in billing-db. This rules out a tariff-rate defect as the cause of the wrong bills, narrowing the "billing rule or tariff defect" explanation floated in E-01's interpretation to the import validation rules side rather than tariff structure.

Field route completion for the Aug-Sep period was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, with 9,200 manual-read accounts affected, showing a real shortfall in manual meter-read completion during the dispute-surge window. No pre-August baseline is given, so this does not by itself establish that completion dropped since August versus a pre-existing gap.

CRM data shows dispute tickets (2,440 of them) are being handled well within the response SLA: median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day target. This indicates the dispute surge's pain point is ticket volume, not response speed/capacity, since existing handling is already meeting its target.
Monthly dispute volume rose from ~600 (Jun/Jul baseline, 610/590) to ~1180-1260 (Aug/Sep), roughly doubling, quantitatively confirming the surge magnitude but saying nothing about its cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (non-authoritative stakeholder claim) states there has been no tariff change this year, which corroborates E-02's authoritative finding of zero logged tariff changes since August and reinforces that tariff-rate structure is not the cause of the wrong bills.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, interview) claims the field-reading team has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers' accounts to fall to estimated bills. This offers a candidate causal mechanism for E-03's observed Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target), but SH-FIELD has a stated incentive toward headcount increase and a bias to attribute problems to staffing, so it needs independent corroboration.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is a contract clause confirming that route priority change requests by the utility must be executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation; it documents the authorization basis already reflected in constraint K-DISPATCH and does not speak to the billing-dispute causal mechanism.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: 320 accounts received estimated bills in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 routes (billing-db, E-09). That volume is far smaller than the 9,200 manual-read accounts affected by the Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (E-03) and the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-01), indicating only a small fraction of lagging routes actually convert to estimated bills.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log's lagging_routes query (E-10, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) identifies 14 specific routes with below-target completion (sample: 0.70 for R-00), giving route-level detail behind the aggregate Aug-Sep shortfall (E-03) from a tool source independent of SH-FIELD's self-interested interview (E-07). It confirms a concrete, bounded set of lagging routes but does not quantify total route population, trend since August, or whether reader staffing specifically is the cause.

U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.question: Has a specific billing import validation rule actually changed around August, and what is the exact defect misclassifying reads/estimates?
U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.decision_impact: Confirms or disconfirms the entire causal mechanism the problem rests on; without it, remediation targeting billing-config could be misdirected.
U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule change log for entries dated around August and correlate timing/content with the disputed-bill read-type pattern (E-01).
U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.safe_placeholder: Treat H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as the working diagnostic hypothesis only; take no corrective action until the specific defect is identified in billing-config.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: What do AMI read events (DA-MDMS) show for disputed accounts, and does this corroborate or rule out an AMI-side contribution, given vendor export access is ACCESS_PENDING and mdms-export is DEGRADED?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Without MDMS data, an AMI-side contribution to the misclassification cannot be ruled in or out, limiting confidence in the final diagnosis.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Await ORG-AMI vendor provisioning of mdms-export access; retry query_mdms_read_events once access is restored.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-rule and read-type diagnosis using billing-db/billing-config only; exclude AMI-side data from the diagnosis conclusion until mdms-export access is granted.

U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.question: Does an independent, authoritative source corroborate SH-FIELD's claim of a reader shortage since July, beyond the biased stakeholder interview (E-07)?
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.decision_impact: Determines whether field staffing should be elevated from a secondary assumption to an active contributor requiring its own remediation track.
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.resolution_path: Cross-check E-07 against an authoritative, non-stakeholder source such as route-log historical trends or field services contract staffing records.
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.safe_placeholder: Keep A-FIELD-SHORTAGE-MINOR as the working assumption and do not redirect remediation effort toward field staffing until corroborated.
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.resolution: route-log (E-10) independently identifies 14 specific lagging routes with sub-target completion, providing authoritative tool-level corroboration of a route completion shortfall distinct from SH-FIELD's interview claim, though it still does not confirm reader staffing shortage as the specific cause.

U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.question: Does the CRM ticket volume metric distinguish disputes caused by billing errors from other dispute reasons, so that a drop in raw ticket count reliably reflects bill-correctness improvement?
U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.decision_impact: If ticket volume mixes unrelated dispute reasons, M-DISPUTE-VOL alone could falsely indicate success or failure of the billing-rule remediation.
U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.resolution_path: Check crm-tickets for a dispute-reason/category field; if absent, request tagging be added or use read-type breakdown as a corroborating signal.
U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.safe_placeholder: Report M-DISPUTE-VOL trend alongside the read-type/rule-defect findings rather than as a standalone success signal, pending reason-tagging confirmation.

A-FIELD-SHORTAGE-MINOR.statement: Field reader shortage and the route-completion shortfall are assumed to be a secondary/minority contributor to disputes rather than the dominant mechanism, since most disputed bills use ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED substitutes.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun/Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug/Sep) (E-05).
Majority (~59%) of disputed bills used ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED substitutes, contrary to what a pure estimate-substitution cause would predict (E-01).

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline (Jun/Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug/Sep) (E-05), driven by a defect in billing import validation rules that misclassifies/corrupts meter reads during import — producing incorrect bills across both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED read types (E-01 shows ACTUAL reads are the majority, ~59%, of disputed bills, ruling out estimate-substitution as the dominant cause) — while tariff-rate changes are ruled out as a cause (E-02 shows zero logged tariff changes, corroborated by E-06).
